title.en: Volume 131 Book of Later Zhou 33: Biographies 11 - Liu Hao, Zhang Hang, Zhang Kefu, Yu Dechen, Wang Yan, Shen Wenbing, Hu Zhai, Liu Gun, Jia Wei, Zhao Yanyi, Shen Gou, Li Zhisun, Sun Chen
title.raw: 卷一百三十一 周書22: 列傳十一 劉皞 張沆 張可復 于德辰 王延 申文炳 扈載 劉袞 賈緯 趙延義 沈遘 李知損 孫晟 Volume 131 Book of Later Zhou 33: Biographies 11 - Liu Hao, Zhang Hang, Zhang Kefu, Yu Dechen, Wang Yan, Shen Wenbing, Hu Zhai, Liu Gun, Jia Wei, Zhao Yanyi, Shen Gou, Li Zhisun, Sun Chen

sentences.zh: 劉皞，字克明，晉丞相譙國公句之弟也。

translations.literal: Liu Hao, styled Keming, was the younger brother of Ju Gou, Duke of Qiao and chancellor of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hao, whose style name was Keming, was the younger brother of Ju Gou, Duke of Qiao and chancellor of Jin.

sentences.zh: 句，《晉書》有傳。

translations.literal: Ju has a biography in the 《Book of Jin》.
translations.idiomatic: Ju has a biography in the 《Book of Jin》.

sentences.zh: 皞少離鄉里，唐天祐中，梁將劉鄩襲太原，軍至樂平，時皞客於縣舍，為鄩軍所俘。

translations.literal: Hao in youth left his native place. In the Tianyou era of Tang, the Liang general Liu Yan attacked Taiyuan; the army reached Leping. At that time Hao was lodging at the county guest-house and was captured by Yan's army.
translations.idiomatic: Hao had left his hometown while still young. During the Tianyou reign of Tang, the Liang general Liu Yan raided Taiyuan; when his army reached Leping, Hao was staying at the county guesthouse and was taken prisoner by Yan's troops.

sentences.zh: 謝彥章見之，知其儒者，待之以禮，謂其鄉人劉去非曰：「為君得一宗人。

translations.literal: Xie Yanzhang saw him, knew he was a scholar, treated him with ritual, and said to his fellow townsman Liu Qufei: "I have obtained a clansman for you."
translations.idiomatic: Xie Yanzhang saw him, recognized him as a man of learning, and treated him with courtesy. He told his fellow townsman Liu Qufei, "I have found a kinsman for you."

sentences.zh: 」即令皞見之，去非詢其爵裏，乃親族也，對泣久之，自是隨去非客於彥章門下。

translations.literal: He immediately had Hao presented to him. Qufei inquired about his rank and native place; they were kin. Facing each other they wept for a long time. From then on he followed Qufei as a guest under Yanzhang's patronage.
translations.idiomatic: He had Hao brought before him at once. Qufei asked about his rank and home district and discovered they were relatives; they faced each other and wept for a long while. From that time on Hao followed Qufei as a client in Yanzhang's household.

sentences.zh: 彥章得罪，去非為郢州刺史，皞隨之郡。

translations.literal: Yanzhang fell into guilt; Qufei became prefect of Ying, and Hao followed him to the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanzhang fell from favor, Qufei was appointed prefect of Ying, and Hao accompanied him to the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 莊宗平河洛，去非以嘗從劉守奇歸梁，深懼獲罪，乃棄郡投高季興於荊南，皞累為荊州攝官。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong pacified Heluo. Qufei, because he had once followed Liu Shouqi in submitting to Liang, deeply feared punishment; he abandoned his prefecture and went to Gao Jixing in Jingnan. Hao successively served as acting officials in Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong pacified the Heluo region, Qufei, having once followed Liu Shouqi in defecting to Liang, was deeply afraid of being punished. He abandoned his prefecture and fled to Gao Jixing in Jingnan, while Hao held a series of acting posts in Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 既而兄句明宗朝為學士，遣人召歸。

translations.literal: Before long his elder brother Ju, in the Mingzong reign, became an academician and sent someone to summon him home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his elder brother Ju became a Hanlin academician under Emperor Mingzong and sent for him to return home.

sentences.zh: 梁漢颙鎮鄧州，辟為從事，入為監察御史，歷水部員外郎、史館修撰。

translations.literal: Liang Hanfu was stationed at Dengzhou and recruited him as a staff member. He entered service as investigating censor and successively served as vice director of the Water Ministry and compiler at the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Hanfu, as military commissioner of Dengzhou, recruited him as a staff officer. He entered the capital as investigating censor and later served as vice director of the Water Ministry and compiler at the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 長興末，宰臣趙鳳鎮邢臺，表為節度判官。

translations.literal: At the end of Changxing, chief minister Zhao Feng was stationed at Xingtai and memorialized him as military administration judge.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Changxing era, chief minister Zhao Feng was posted to Xingtai and recommended him as military administration judge.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，入為起居郎，改駕部員外郎，兼侍御史知雜事，移河南少尹、兵部郎中，轉太府卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai he entered as court diarist, was changed to vice director of the Chariotry Ministry, and concurrently served as attendant censor in charge of miscellaneous matters; he was moved to vice commissioner of Henan, director of the Bingsbu, and transferred to grand steward of the Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Qingtai era he entered court service as diarist, was reassigned as vice director of the Chariotry Ministry, and concurrently served as attendant censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs. He was then appointed vice commissioner of Henan, director of the Ministry of War, and finally grand steward of the Treasury.

sentences.zh: 漢祖受命，用為宗正卿。

translations.literal: When the Han founder received the Mandate, he was used as Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: When the founder of Later Han took the throne, he was appointed Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 周初，改衛尉卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhou he was changed to Director of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Later Zhou he was reassigned as Director of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 廣順元年冬十月，稅居於東京，夜夢鬼詫之曰：「公於我冢上安床，深不奉益。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter in the first year of Guangshun, while renting a residence in the Eastern Capital, at night he dreamed a ghost reproached him, saying: "You have placed your bed on my grave mound — deeply not respectful."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter in the first year of Guangshun, while renting a house in the Eastern Capital, he dreamed at night that a ghost reproached him: "You have set your bed on my grave mound — a grave disrespect."

sentences.zh: 」皞問鬼姓氏，曰李丕文。

translations.literal: Hao asked the ghost's surname; it said Li Piwen.
translations.idiomatic: Hao asked the ghost's surname; it replied, "Li Piwen."

sentences.zh: 皞曰：「君言殊誤，都城內豈可冢耶？

translations.literal: Hao said: "What you say is quite mistaken — how could there be a grave mound inside the capital city?"
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "You are quite mistaken — how could there be a burial mound inside the capital?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「冢本在野，張十八郎展城時圍入。

translations.literal: It said: "The grave mound was originally in the countryside; when Officer Zhang the Eighteenth expanded the walls, it was enclosed within."
translations.idiomatic: It answered, "The mound was originally in the open country; when Officer Zhang the Eighteenth expanded the city walls, it was taken inside."

sentences.zh: 」忽寤。

translations.literal: He suddenly awoke.
translations.idiomatic: He woke with a start.

sentences.zh: 又半月，復夢前鬼曰：「公不相信，屈觀吾舍可乎？

translations.literal: Another half-month later he again dreamed the former ghost, who said: "Since you do not believe, would you condescend to visit my dwelling?"
translations.idiomatic: Half a month later he dreamed of the same ghost again, who said, "Since you do not believe me, would you be so kind as to visit my house?"

sentences.zh: 」即以手掊地，豁然見華第，花木叢萃，房廊雕煥，立皞於西廡。

translations.literal: It then with its hand broke open the ground; a magnificent mansion suddenly appeared, with flowers and trees clustered together and corridors and chambers carved and splendid; it placed Hao in the west wing.
translations.idiomatic: With its hand it broke open the ground, and a splendid mansion suddenly appeared, its flowers and trees thickly clustered and its halls and corridors carved and bright. It set Hao down in the west gallery.

sentences.zh: 久之，見一團火如電，前來漸近，即前鬼也。

translations.literal: After a long while he saw a ball of fire like lightning coming from before, drawing nearer and nearer — it was the former ghost.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he saw a ball of fire like lightning approaching from the distance — it was the same ghost as before.

sentences.zh: 引皞深入，出其孥，泣拜如有所托。

translations.literal: It led Hao deep within, brought out its wife and children, and they wept and bowed as though entrusting someone with a charge.
translations.idiomatic: It led Hao deeper inside, brought out its wife and children, and they wept and bowed as though placing someone in their trust.

sentences.zh: 皞問丕文鬼事，曰：「冥司各有部屬，外不知也。

translations.literal: Hao asked about Piwen's affairs in the ghost realm; it said: "Each department in the Nether Bureau has its own jurisdiction; outsiders do not know."
translations.idiomatic: Hao asked about Piwen's affairs in the underworld; it said, "Each office in the Nether Bureau has its own jurisdiction — outsiders cannot know."

sentences.zh: 」皞曰：「余官何至？

translations.literal: Hao said: "To what office will I rise?"
translations.idiomatic: Hao asked, "To what office will I rise?"

sentences.zh: 」再三不對，苦訊之，曰：「齊王判官。

translations.literal: Repeatedly it would not answer; when he pressed hard in questioning, it said: "Aide to the Prince of Qi."
translations.idiomatic: It refused to answer again and again; when he pressed it hard, it said, "Aide to the Prince of Qi."

sentences.zh: 」皞曰：「張令公為齊王，去世久矣。

translations.literal: Hao said: "Director Zhang served as Prince of Qi and died long ago."
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "Director Zhang was Prince of Qi, and he died long ago."

sentences.zh: 今鄆州高令公為齊王，余方為列卿，豈復為賓佐乎？

translations.literal: Now High Director at Yanzhou is Prince of Qi; I am presently a minister of the nine courts — how could I again become a client's aide?"
translations.idiomatic: Now High Director at Yanzhou is Prince of Qi, and I am presently a minister of the nine courts — how could I again become someone's staff aide?"

sentences.zh: 」鬼曰：「不知也。

translations.literal: The ghost said: "I do not know."
translations.idiomatic: The ghost said, "I do not know."

sentences.zh: 」皞既寤，欲掘而視之。

translations.literal: When Hao awoke he wished to dig and look.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao awoke, he wanted to dig there and see for himself.

sentences.zh: 既而又告人曰：「鬼雖見訴，其如吾稅舍何？

translations.literal: Yet he also told people: "Though the ghost has pleaded its case, what of my rented dwelling?"
translations.idiomatic: But then he told others, "The ghost may have pleaded its case, but what am I to do about my rented house?"

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: So he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: So he dropped the idea.

sentences.zh: 廣順二年春，朝廷以皞為高麗冊使。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year of Guangshun, the court appointed Hao envoy to invest Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Guangshun, the court appointed Hao envoy to invest the king of Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 三月，至鄆，節度使高行周以皞嗜酒，留連累日，旦夕沈醉。

translations.literal: In the third month he reached Yan; Military Commissioner Gao Xingzhou, because Hao was fond of wine, detained him for many days, morning and evening sunk in drunkenness.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he reached Yan, where Military Commissioner Gao Xingzhou, knowing Hao's love of wine, kept him for many days on end, drinking himself into a stupor morning and night.

sentences.zh: 其月二十三日，晨興櫛發，狀如醉寐，男泳視之，已卒矣。

translations.literal: On the twenty-third day of that month, when he rose in the morning to comb his hair, he appeared as if drunk and sleeping; his son Yong looked at him and he was already dead.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-third day of that month, when he rose in the morning to comb his hair, he looked as though drunk and asleep; his son Yong looked in on him and found him already dead.

translations.literal: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.
translations.idiomatic: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.

sentences.zh: （《太平廣記》云：銜命使吳越，路由鄆州，卒於郵亭。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Extensive Records of the Taiping Era》 says: While on mission to Wuyue, passing through Yanzhou, he died at the courier station.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Extensive Records of the Taiping Era》 states: While on an imperial mission to Wuyue, he passed through Yanzhou and died at a courier station.)〉

sentences.zh: 時年六十一。

translations.literal: He was at that time sixty-one years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was sixty-one years old.

sentences.zh: 其年八月，鄆帥齊王高行周亦夢鬼請齊王判官，得無是乎！

translations.literal: In the eighth month of that year the Yan commander Prince of Qi Gao Xingzhou also dreamed of a ghost requesting the Prince of Qi's aide — could it not have been this!
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of that year the Yan commander, Prince of Qi Gao Xingzhou, also dreamed of a ghost requesting the Prince of Qi's aide — could this not have been the same affair!

sentences.zh: 皞從儒學，好聚書，嗜酒無儀檢，然衷抱無他，急於行義，士友以此多之。

translations.literal: Hao followed Confucian learning, loved to collect books, was fond of wine and without ritual decorum, yet in his inner heart he harbored no other designs and was urgent in acting righteously; scholar-friends for this reason held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Hao had devoted himself to classical learning, loved to collect books, and was fond of wine and careless of decorum, yet he harbored no hidden designs and was quick to act on principle; for this reason his scholarly friends held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 張沆，字太元，徐州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Hang, styled Taiyuan, was a man of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hang, whose style name was Taiyuan, was a native of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 父嚴，本州牙將。

translations.literal: His father Yan was a military adjutant of his native prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan had been a military adjutant in their home prefecture.

sentences.zh: 沆少力學，攻詞賦，登進士第。

translations.literal: Hang in youth applied himself to study, devoted himself to poetic prose, and passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Hang applied himself diligently to study, specialized in regulated verse and fu, and passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 唐明宗子秦王好文，然童年疏率，動不由禮。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin, son of Emperor Mingzong of Tang, loved literature, yet in childhood was careless and casual; his actions seldom followed propriety.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin, a son of Emperor Mingzong of Tang, loved literature, but even as a boy he was careless and impulsive, and his conduct seldom accorded with propriety.

sentences.zh: 每賓僚大集，手自出題，令面前賦詩，少不如意，則壞裂抵棄。

translations.literal: Whenever guest officials gathered in great assembly, he would hand out topics himself and order them to compose poetry on the spot; if anything was slightly unsatisfactory, he would tear and throw it away.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever his guests and staff assembled in large numbers, he would set topics himself and order them to compose poetry on the spot; if anything fell even slightly short of his liking, he would tear it up and cast it aside.

sentences.zh: 沆初以刺謁，秦王屬合座客各為《南湖廳記》，因謂沆曰：「聞生名久矣，請為此文。

translations.literal: Hang at first presented a memorial to gain access; the Prince of Qin ordered all seated guests each to compose a 《Record of the South Lake Hall》, and said to Hang: "I have long heard your name — please write this piece."
translations.idiomatic: Hang first gained access by presenting a memorial. The Prince of Qin ordered every guest at the gathering to compose a 《Record of the South Lake Hall》 and said to Hang, "I have long heard your name — please write this piece for us."

sentences.zh: 」沆不獲已，從之。

translations.literal: Hang, unable to refuse, complied.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to refuse, Hang complied.

sentences.zh: 及群士記成，獨取沆所為勒之於石，繇是署為河南府巡官。

translations.literal: When the gathered scholars' compositions were complete, he alone took Hang's work and had it carved on stone; on this account he was appointed touring officer of Henan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the scholars' compositions were finished, the prince took only Hang's essay and had it carved in stone; on this account Hang was appointed touring officer of the Henan prefectural government.

sentences.zh: 秦王敗，勒歸鄉里。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qin was defeated, the inscription was compelled to return to his native district.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qin was defeated, the inscription was removed and Hang returned to his hometown.

sentences.zh: 晉初，桑維翰秉政，沆以文幹進，用為著作佐郎、集賢校理，遷右拾遺。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin, Sang Weihan held power; Hang advanced by literary talent and was used as assistant compiler, collator at the Jixian Institute, and promoted to right remonstrance official.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jin dynasty Sang Weihan held power; Hang advanced on the strength of his literary ability and was appointed assistant compiler and collator at the Jixian Institute, then promoted to right remonstrance official.

sentences.zh: 維翰出鎮，奏為記室。

translations.literal: When Weihan went out to command a circuit, he memorialized for him as secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Weihan went out to command a military circuit, he recommended Hang as his secretary.

sentences.zh: 從維翰入朝，授殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Following Weihan into court, he was appointed palace attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: When he followed Weihan back to court, he was appointed palace attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，自侍御史改祠部員外郎知制誥，召入翰林為學士。

translations.literal: After a year more he changed from attendant censor to vice director of the Ancestral Temple Ministry with drafting duties and was summoned into the Hanlin as academician.
translations.idiomatic: A little more than a year later he was transferred from attendant censor to vice director of the Ancestral Temple Ministry with responsibility for drafting edicts, and was summoned into the Hanlin Academy as an academician.

sentences.zh: 維翰罷相，馮玉用事，不欲沆居禁密，改右諫議大夫，罷其職。

translations.literal: When Weihan left the chancellorship, Feng Yu held power and did not wish Hang to remain in the inner secretariat; he was changed to right remonstrance official and his duties were removed.
translations.idiomatic: When Weihan left the chancellorship, Feng Yu came to power and did not want Hang in the inner secretariat; Hang was reassigned as right remonstrance official and removed from his Hanlin post.

sentences.zh: 漢祖至汴，轉右常侍，復用為學士，未幾，遷工部尚書充職。

translations.literal: When the Han founder reached Bian, he was transferred to right regular attendant, again used as academician; before long promoted to Minister of Works while retaining the post.
translations.idiomatic: When the founder of Later Han reached Bian, Hang was transferred to right regular attendant and again appointed Hanlin academician; before long he was promoted to Minister of Works while retaining that post.

sentences.zh: 明年，以營奉葬事求解職，改禮部尚書。

translations.literal: The next year, citing duty in arranging imperial burial affairs, he requested to leave office and was changed to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, citing his duty in arranging imperial burial affairs, he asked to be relieved of his Hanlin duties and was reassigned as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 及歸朝，復為學士。

translations.literal: When he returned to court he again served as academician.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to court he was again made a Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 太祖以沆耳疾罷職，改刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Taizu, because of Hang's ear ailment, removed him from office and changed him to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu removed him from the Hanlin post because of his ear ailment and reassigned him as Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 廣順二年秋，命為故齊王高行周冊贈使，復命而卒。

translations.literal: In autumn of the second year of Guangshun he was ordered envoy to confer posthumous honors on the former Prince of Qi Gao Xingzhou; he returned from his mission and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the second year of Guangshun he was appointed envoy to confer posthumous honors on the former Prince of Qi, Gao Xingzhou; he returned from his mission and died.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 沆性儒雅，好釋氏，雖久居祿位，家無餘財，死之日，圖書之外，唯使鄆之資耳。

translations.literal: Hang's nature was refined and courteous; he loved Buddhism. Though he long held salary rank, the household had no surplus property; on the day of his death, apart from books, there was only his envoy's allowance from Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Hang was refined and courteous by nature and fond of Buddhism. Though he had long held salaried office, his household had no surplus wealth; on the day of his death, apart from his books, all he left was the allowance from his mission to Yan.

sentences.zh: 嗣子尚幼，親友慮其耗散，上言於太祖，乃令三司差人主葬，余資市邸舍，以贍其孤焉。

translations.literal: His heir son was still young; relatives and friends feared the property would be dissipated and petitioned Taizu; then the Three Offices dispatched men to manage the burial, and the remaining funds were used to buy townhouses to support the orphan.
translations.idiomatic: His heir was still a child, and relatives and friends feared the estate would be squandered; they petitioned Taizu, who ordered the Three Offices to send men to manage the burial and use the remaining funds to buy townhouses to support the orphan.

sentences.zh: 沆記覽文史，好征求僻事，公家應用，時出一聯以炫奇筆，故不為馮玉所重。

translations.literal: Hang's memory embraced literature and history; he loved to seek out obscure facts; for official use he would sometimes produce a couplet to display his remarkable brush — therefore he was not esteemed by Feng Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Hang had a wide memory for literature and history and loved to hunt out obscure facts; for official documents he would sometimes produce a striking couplet to show off his unusual talent, and for this reason Feng Yu did not hold him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 雖有聵疾，猶出入金門，凡五六年。

translations.literal: Though he had deafness, he still went in and out of the Golden Gate for some five or six years.
translations.idiomatic: Though he suffered from deafness, he still went in and out of the palace gates for some five or six years.

sentences.zh: 漢隱帝末年，楊、史遇害，翌日，沆方知之，聽猶未審，忽問同僚曰：「竊聞盜殺史公，其盜獲否？

translations.literal: In the final year of Emperor Yin of Han, when Yang and Shi were murdered, the next day Hang only then learned of it; his hearing had still not recovered — he suddenly asked his colleagues: "I have heard in secret that robbers killed Director Shi — have the robbers been captured?"
translations.idiomatic: In the final year of Emperor Yin of Later Han, when Yang and Shi were murdered, Hang learned of it only the next day. His hearing had still not cleared, and he suddenly asked his colleagues, "I have heard in secret that robbers killed Director Shi — have the robbers been caught?"

sentences.zh: 」是時京師恟懼之次，聞者笑之。

translations.literal: At that time the capital was in the midst of panic and fear; those who heard laughed.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment the capital was in the grip of panic and fear, and those who heard him could only laugh.

sentences.zh: 有士人申光遜者，與沆友善，沆未病時，夢沆手出小佛塔示光遜，視其上有詩十四字云：「今生不見故人面，明月高高上翠樓。

translations.literal: There was a scholar Shen Guangxun who was friendly with Hang; before Hang fell ill, he dreamed Hang took out a small Buddhist pagoda to show Guangxun; looking at it, upon it was a poem of fourteen characters: "In this life I shall not see an old friend's face; the bright moon rises high above the green tower."
translations.idiomatic: A scholar named Shen Guangxun was on friendly terms with Hang. Before Hang fell ill, Guangxun dreamed that Hang took out a small Buddhist pagoda and showed it to him; on it was a poem of fourteen characters: "In this life I shall not see an old friend's face; the bright moon climbs high above the green tower."

sentences.zh: 」光遜既寤，心惡之，俄聞沆卒。

translations.literal: When Guangxun awoke he was displeased by it; soon he heard Hang had died.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangxun awoke he was troubled by the dream; before long he heard that Hang had died.

sentences.zh: 張可復，字伯恭，德州平原人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Kefu, styled Bogong, was a man of Pingyuan in Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kefu, whose style name was Bogong, was a native of Pingyuan in Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 父達，累贈戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Da was repeatedly posthumously enfeoffed Vice Minister of the Household Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: His father Da was repeatedly granted posthumous enfeoffment as Vice Minister of the Household Ministry.

sentences.zh: 可復略通儒術，少習吏事。

translations.literal: Kefu had slight mastery of Confucian learning and in youth studied clerical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Kefu had a modest grasp of Confucian learning and in his youth trained in clerical work.

sentences.zh: 梁末，薄遊於魏，鄴王羅紹威表為安陽簿。

translations.literal: At the end of Liang he traveled briefly in Wei; the Prince of Ye Luo Shaowei memorialized him as recorder of Anyang.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Liang he traveled briefly in Wei, where the Prince of Ye, Luo Shaowei, recommended him as recorder of Anyang.

sentences.zh: 唐天成初，依晉公霍彥威於青州，為從事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng in Tang he attached himself to Duke Jin Huo Yanwei at Qingzhou as a staff member.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tiancheng era he entered the service of Duke Jin Huo Yanwei at Qingzhou as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 晉公以其滑稽好避事，目為「奸兔兒」。

translations.literal: The Duke Jin, because he was facetious and good at avoiding responsibility, nicknamed him "the crafty rabbit."
translations.idiomatic: The duke, finding him witty but fond of shirking responsibility, nicknamed him "the crafty rabbit."

sentences.zh: 長興中入朝，拜監察御史，六遷至兵部郎中，賜金紫。

translations.literal: In the Changxing era he entered court and was appointed investigating censor; after six promotions he reached director of the Bingsbu and was granted the gold seal and purple sash.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changxing era he entered court service and was appointed investigating censor; after six promotions he reached director of the Ministry of War and was granted the gold seal and purple sash.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，自西京留守判官入為秘書少監，改左司郎中。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu era of Jin, from judicial administrator of the Western Capital's military governor he entered service as vice director of the Secretariat and was changed to director of the Left Department.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianfu era of Later Jin he moved from judicial administrator under the Western Capital's military governor to vice director of the Secretariat, then to director of the Left Department.

sentences.zh: 開運中，遷左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyun era he was promoted to left remonstrance official.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyun era he was promoted to left remonstrance official.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐初，湘陰公鎮徐方，朝行中選可以從戎者，因授武寧軍節度副使、檢校禮部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyou in Han, when the Duke of Xiangyin was military commissioner at Xuzhou, the court selected from the traveling ranks those who could follow the army and accordingly appointed him vice military commissioner of Wuning circuit and acting Minister of Rites with inspection duties.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qianyou era of Later Han, when the Duke of Xiangyin was military commissioner at Xuzhou, the court chose from among the traveling officials those fit for military service and accordingly appointed Kefu vice military commissioner of Wuning circuit and acting Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 及世宗鎮澶淵，改鎮寧軍節度行軍司馬。

translations.literal: When Shizong was stationed at Chanyuan he was changed to military expedition secretary of Zhenning circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Shizong was posted at Chanyuan, Kefu was reassigned as military expedition secretary of Zhenning circuit.

sentences.zh: 三年，征拜給事中。

translations.literal: In the third year he was summoned and appointed vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was summoned to court and appointed vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，以澶淵幕府之舊，拜右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Shizong succeeded to the throne, because of old ties from the Chanyuan staff, he was appointed right attendant at large.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong succeeded to the throne, in recognition of their old ties from the Chanyuan staff, he was appointed right attendant at large.

sentences.zh: 顯德元年秋，以疾卒，年七十有三。

translations.literal: In autumn of the first year of Xiande he died of illness, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the first year of Xiande he died of illness at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 制贈戶部尚書。

translations.literal: By edict he was posthumously enfeoffed Minister of the Household Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial edict he was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of the Household Ministry.

sentences.zh: 可復無他才，惟以謹願保長年，加之迂懦，多為同列輕俊者所侮，而累階至金紫，居三品之秩，亦其命耶！

translations.literal: Kefu had no other talent; only through cautious dutifulness he preserved a long life, and moreover he was obtuse and timid — he was often insulted by colleagues who were light and sharp, yet he rose step by step to the gold seal and purple sash and the rank of the third grade; was this also his fate!
translations.idiomatic: Kefu had no other talent; he preserved a long life solely through cautious dutifulness, and moreover he was dull and timid, so that colleagues who were quick and sharp often looked down on him. Yet he rose step by step to the gold seal and purple sash and the third rank of office — was this too simply his allotted fate!

sentences.zh: 於德辰，字進明，元城人也。

translations.literal: Yu Dechen, styled Jinming, was a man of Yuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Dechen, whose style name was Jinming, was a native of Yuancheng.

sentences.zh: 幼敏悟，篤誌好學，及射策文場，數上不調。

translations.literal: In youth he was keen and perceptive, devoted in aspiration and fond of learning; at the literary examination grounds he several times failed to pass.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was quick and perceptive, devoted in aspiration and fond of study, but at the civil examination he failed to pass several times in succession.

sentences.zh: 後唐明宗鎮邢州，德辰往謁焉，明宗見而器之，因得假官於屬邑。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingzong of Later Tang was stationed at Xingzhou, Dechen went to visit him; Mingzong saw him and valued him, and accordingly obtained a provisional appointment in a subordinate county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingzong of Later Tang was posted to Xingzhou, Dechen went to visit him. Mingzong took notice of him and valued his ability, and Dechen thereby obtained a provisional appointment in a subordinate county.

sentences.zh: 後繼歷州縣，歷仕晉、漢、周，官至工部尚書。

translations.literal: Thereafter he successively served in prefectures and counties, served through Jin, Han, and Zhou, and reached the office of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to serve in a series of prefectural and county posts through the Jin, Han, and Zhou dynasties, eventually rising to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 王延，字世美，鄚州長豐人也。

translations.literal: Wang Yan, styled Shimei, was a man of Changfeng in Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan, whose style name was Shimei, was a native of Changfeng in Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 少為儒，善詞賦，會鄉曲離亂，不獲從鄉薦，因客於浮陽，隨滄帥戴思遠入梁。

translations.literal: In youth he studied as a Confucian and was skilled in poetic prose; when his native district was torn by chaos he could not obtain nomination through the village recommendation, so he traveled as a guest to Fuyang and followed the Cangzhou commander Dai Siyuan into Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he studied the classics and excelled at regulated verse and fu. When his home district was thrown into chaos he could not obtain local nomination for office, so he went as a client to Fuyang and followed the Cangzhou commander Dai Siyuan into Liang territory.

sentences.zh: 嘗以所為賦謁梁相李琪，琪覽之，欣然曰：「此道近難其人，王生升我堂矣。

translations.literal: He once presented a fu he had written to Liang chancellor Li Qi; Qi read it and said with pleasure: "In this craft it has lately been hard to find the right person — Master Wang has raised me to the hall level."
translations.idiomatic: He once presented a fu he had written to the Liang chancellor Li Qi. Qi read it and said with delight, "In this art it has lately been hard to find the right man — Master Wang has raised me to the hall."

sentences.zh: 」繇是人士稱之。

translations.literal: From this men of letters praised him.
translations.idiomatic: From that time men of letters spoke highly of him.

sentences.zh: 尋薦為即墨縣令，歷徐、宋、鄆、青四鎮從事。

translations.literal: Soon he was recommended as magistrate of Jimo and successively served as staff member at the four circuits of Xu, Song, Yan, and Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recommended as magistrate of Jimo and went on to serve as staff officer at the four military circuits of Xu, Song, Yan, and Qing.

sentences.zh: 長興初，鄉人馮道、趙鳳在相位，擢拜左補闕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changxing, his fellow townsman Feng Dao and Zhao Feng held chancellorships and promoted him to left remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Changxing era his fellow townsman Feng Dao and Zhao Feng held the chancellorship and promoted him to left remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 逾年，以水部員外知制誥遷中書舍人，賜金紫。

translations.literal: After a year he was moved as vice director of Water with drafting duties to central secretariat drafter and granted the gold seal and purple sash.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was promoted from vice director of the Water Ministry with drafting duties to central secretariat drafter and granted the gold seal and purple sash.

sentences.zh: 清泰末，以本官權知貢舉。

translations.literal: At the end of Qingtai he held his original office with provisional charge of the civil service examination.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Qingtai era he retained his original post while given provisional charge of the civil service examination.

sentences.zh: 時有舉子崔頎者，故相協之子也。

translations.literal: At that time there was an examinee named Cui Hao, son of the former chancellor Xie.
translations.idiomatic: At that time one of the candidates was Cui Hao, son of the former chancellor Cui Xie.

sentences.zh: 協素與吏部尚書盧文紀不睦，及延將入貢院，文紀謂延曰：「舍人以謹重聞於時，所以去冬老夫在相位時，與諸相首以長者聞奏，用掌文衡。

translations.literal: Xie had long been on bad terms with Minister of Personnel Lu Wennji; when Yan was about to enter the examination hall, Wennji said to Yan: "As drafter you are known to the age for caution and weight — therefore last winter when I the elder was in the chancellorship, together with the other chancellors we first reported you to the throne as a man of standing, using you to manage the standards of literature."
translations.idiomatic: Xie had long been at odds with Minister of Personnel Lu Wennji. As Yan was about to enter the examination compound, Wennji said to him, "As a drafter you are known throughout the realm for your caution and gravity. That is why last winter, when I was still in the chancellorship, the other chief ministers and I first reported you to the throne as a man of standing and entrusted you with the literary examinations."

sentences.zh: 然貢闈取士，頗多面目。

translations.literal: Yet in the examination compound, selecting scholars, there are quite many faces shown.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the examination hall, when selecting candidates, there is all too much favoritism shown to familiar faces.

sentences.zh: 說者云：『越人善泅，生子方晬，乳母浮之水上。

translations.literal: It is said: "The Yue people are skilled at swimming; when a child is one month old, the wet-nurse floats him on the water."
translations.idiomatic: People say, "The people of Yue are skilled swimmers; when a child is barely a month old, the wet-nurse floats him on the water."

sentences.zh: 或駭然止之，乳母曰，其父善泅，子必無溺。

translations.literal: Some, startled, would stop her; the wet-nurse said, his father is skilled at swimming — the child certainly will not drown.
translations.idiomatic: Some onlookers, alarmed, would try to stop her, but the wet-nurse would say, "His father is a skilled swimmer — the child will certainly not drown."

sentences.zh: 』今若以名下取士，即此類也。

translations.literal: 'If one now selects scholars by patronage, it is just this sort of thing.'
translations.idiomatic: 'If candidates are chosen by patronage and connections rather than merit, it is exactly this sort of thing.'

sentences.zh: 舍人當求實才，以副公望。

translations.literal: The Gentleman-in-Attendance should seek real talent, to fulfill the public expectation.
translations.idiomatic: As drafter, you should seek genuine talent, to meet the expectations placed upon you.

sentences.zh: 」延退而謂人曰：「盧公之言，蓋為崔頎也。

translations.literal: Yan withdrew and said to people: "Lord Lu's words were probably aimed at Cui Hao.
translations.idiomatic: After Yan withdrew, he said to others, "Lord Lu's remarks were surely directed at Cui Hao.

sentences.zh: 縱與其父不悅，致意何至此耶！

translations.literal: Even if he bears ill will toward the father, why would his message go this far!
translations.idiomatic: Even if he is displeased with the father, why would he go so far in making his point!

sentences.zh: 」來春，以頎登甲科。

translations.literal: The next spring, Hao passed the examination in the top tier.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring, Hao passed the examinations with the highest rank.

sentences.zh: 其年，改御史中丞，歲滿，轉尚書右丞。

translations.literal: That year he was changed to Assistant Censor-in-Chief; when his term expired, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Right in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was appointed Assistant Censor-in-Chief; when his term expired, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Right in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 奉使兩浙，吳人深重之。

translations.literal: Sent on mission to the Two Zhes, the Wu people held him in deep esteem.
translations.idiomatic: While on an imperial mission to the Two Zhes, the people of Wu held him in the highest regard.

sentences.zh: 復命，授吏部侍郎，改尚書左丞，拜太常卿，歷工、禮、刑三尚書。

translations.literal: Upon returning from his mission, he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel, changed to Vice Director of the Left in the Secretariat, invested as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and successively served as Minister of Works, Minister of Rites, and Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: After he reported back from his mission, he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel, then reassigned as Vice Director of the Left in the Secretariat, invested as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and later served in succession as Minister of Works, Minister of Rites, and Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 以疾求分司西洛，授太子少保。

translations.literal: Because of illness he requested a supernumerary post in the Western Capital at Luoyang and was appointed Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: On grounds of illness he requested a supernumerary post in the Western Capital at Luoyang and was appointed Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 既而連月請告，為留臺所糾，改少傅致仕。

translations.literal: Before long he requested sick leave month after month and was impeached by the Luoyang supervisory office; he was changed to Junior Preceptor and granted retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he took sick leave month after month and was censured by the Luoyang supervisory office; he was reassigned as Junior Preceptor and granted retirement.

sentences.zh: 廣順二年冬卒，時年七十有三。

translations.literal: In winter of the second year of Guangshun he died, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the winter of the second year of Guangshun, at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 子億，仕皇朝為殿中丞。

translations.literal: His son Yi served the Great Dynasty as Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi served the Song court as Palace Censor.

sentences.zh: 申文炳，字國華，洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Shen Wenbing, styled Guohua, was a man of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Wenbing, whose style name was Guohua, was a native of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 父鄂，唐左千牛衛將軍。

translations.literal: His father E was Left General of the Thousand-Ox Guard of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: His father E had been Left General of the Thousand-Ox Guard under Tang.

sentences.zh: 文炳長興中進士擢第，釋褐中正軍節度推官，歷孟、懷支使，鄆城、陜縣二邑宰，自澶州觀察判官入為右補闕。

translations.literal: Wenbing passed the jinshi examination in the Changxing era, upon leaving coarse cloth became military administration judge under the Zhongzheng Army military commissioner, successively served as branch commissioner of Meng and Huai, magistrate of the two districts of Yuncheng and Shanxian, and from observation commissioner judge at Cao Prefecture entered court as Right Remonstrance and Supplementation Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing passed the jinshi examination in the Changxing era. Upon taking his first office he became military administration judge on the staff of the Zhongzheng Army military commissioner, later served as branch commissioner in Meng and Huai, and as magistrate of Yuncheng and Shanxian. From his post as observation commissioner judge at Cao Prefecture he entered the capital as Right Remonstrance and Supplementation Officer.

sentences.zh: 晉開運初，授虞部員外知制誥，轉金部郎中充職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyun in Jin he was appointed Vice Director of the Revenues Ministry with charge of drafting edicts, and was transferred to Director of the Gold Ministry while retaining that duty.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaiyun era of Later Jin he was appointed Vice Director of the Revenues Ministry with charge of drafting edicts, and was then transferred to Director of the Gold Ministry while continuing in that drafting role.

sentences.zh: 廣順中，為學士，遷中書舍人、知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the Guangshun era he became an academician, was promoted to Secretariat Drafter and given charge of the civil service examination.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangshun era he became a Hanlin academician, was promoted to Secretariat Drafter, and was put in charge of the civil service examination.

translations.literal: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.
translations.idiomatic: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.

sentences.zh: （《玉壺清話》：李慶，顯德中舉進士，工詩，有云：「醉輕浮世事，老重故鄉人。

translations.literal: (The 《Jade Pot Pure Conversations》 says: Li Qing, in the Xiande era passed the jinshi examination and was skilled at poetry; he had a line: "When drunk, I lightly float past worldly affairs; in old age, I deeply cherish people from my homeland."
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Jade Pot Pure Conversations》 states: Li Qing passed the jinshi examination in the Xiande era and was skilled at poetry. He wrote a couplet: "When drunk, I lightly float past the affairs of the world; in old age, I deeply cherish the people of my homeland."

sentences.zh: 」樞密王樸以此一聯薦於申文炳。

translations.literal: Grand Councilor Wang Pu recommended this couplet to Shen Wenbing.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Wang Pu recommended this couplet to Shen Wenbing.

sentences.zh: 文炳知貢舉，遂為第三人。）〉

translations.literal: Wenbing, in charge of the examination, then placed him third. )〉
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing, who was in charge of the examination, then placed him third among the successful candidates.)〉

sentences.zh: 顯德五年秋，以疾解職，授左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In autumn of the fifth year of Xiande, because of illness he resigned his office and was appointed Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fifth year of Xiande he resigned on grounds of illness and was appointed Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 六年秋，卒於家，時年五十。

translations.literal: In autumn of the sixth year he died at home, aged fifty.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the sixth year he died at home at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 文炳為文典雅，有訓誥之風。

translations.literal: Wenbing's writing was refined and elegant, with the style of imperial admonitions and investitures.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing wrote in a refined and elegant style, with the dignified tone of imperial admonitions and investitures.

sentences.zh: 執性紓緩，待搢紳以禮，中年而卒，皆惜之。

translations.literal: His disposition was easy and unhurried, and he treated gentry with ritual propriety; he died in middle age, and all regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: His manner was easy and unhurried, and he treated the gentry with courtesy. He died in middle age, and all who knew him mourned the loss.

sentences.zh: 扈載，少好學，善屬文，賦頌碑贊尤其所長。

translations.literal: Hu Zai in youth loved learning, was skilled at literary composition, and was especially accomplished in fu, eulogies, stele inscriptions, and encomia.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Zai loved learning from youth, excelled at literary composition, and was especially gifted in fu, eulogies, stele inscriptions, and encomia.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，隨計於禮部，文價為一時之最，是歲升高等。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he went up for the examination at the Ministry of Rites; the value placed on his writing was the highest of the age, and that year he passed in the upper tier.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Guangshun era he traveled to the capital for the Ministry of Rites examination. His literary reputation was the finest of the day, and that year he passed in the upper tier.

sentences.zh: 載因遊相國寺，見庭竹可愛，作《碧鮮賦》題其壁。

translations.literal: Zai, while visiting Xiangguo Temple, saw the courtyard bamboo and found it lovely; he wrote the 《Fresh Green Fu》 and inscribed it on the wall.
translations.idiomatic: While visiting Xiangguo Temple, Zai saw the courtyard bamboo and was charmed by it. He composed the 《Fresh Green Fu》 and inscribed it on the wall.

sentences.zh: 世宗聞之，遣小黃門就壁錄之，覽而稱善，因拜水部員外郎知制誥，遷翰林學士，賜緋。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong heard of it, sent a palace attendant to copy it from the wall, read it and praised it, and accordingly invested him as Vice Director of the Water Ministry with charge of drafting edicts, promoted him to Hanlin Academician, and bestowed crimson robes.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong heard of it, he sent a palace attendant to copy the text from the wall. After reading it he praised it and accordingly appointed Zai Vice Director of the Water Ministry with charge of drafting edicts, promoted him to Hanlin Academician, and granted him crimson robes.

translations.literal: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.
translations.idiomatic: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.

sentences.zh: （《宋史·李蒨傳》：扈載以文章馳名，樞密使王樸薦令知制誥，除書未下，樸詣中書言之，蒨曰：「斯人命薄，慮不克享耳。

translations.literal: (The 《History of Song · Biography of Li Qian》 says: Hu Zai was famed for his writing; Grand Councilor Wang Pu recommended him for charge of drafting edicts. Before the appointment decree had been issued, Pu went to the Secretariat to speak of it. Qian said: "This man's fate is thin; I fear he will not be able to enjoy the appointment."
translations.idiomatic: (The 《History of Song · Biography of Li Qian》 states: Hu Zai was renowned for his literary talent, and Grand Councilor Wang Pu recommended him for charge of drafting edicts. Before the appointment decree had been issued, Pu went to the Secretariat to discuss the matter. Qian said, "This man's fate is slight; I fear he will not live to enjoy the appointment."

sentences.zh: 」樸曰：「公在衡石之地，當以材進人，何得言命而遺才。

translations.literal: Pu said: "Sir, in the place of weights and measures, you ought to advance men by talent — how can you speak of fate and leave talent behind?"
translations.idiomatic: Pu replied, "Sir, in your position of power you ought to advance men on the basis of talent. How can you speak of fate and leave talent unused?"

sentences.zh: 」載遂知制誥、遷翰林學士，未幾卒。

translations.literal: Zai then received charge of drafting edicts and was promoted to Hanlin Academician; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Zai was then given charge of drafting edicts and promoted to Hanlin Academician, but before long he died.

sentences.zh: 世謂樸能薦士，蒨能知人。）〉

translations.literal: The age said that Pu could recommend scholars and Qian could discern men. )〉
translations.idiomatic: People of the time said that Pu knew how to recommend talent and Qian knew how to read men.)〉

sentences.zh: 而載已病，不能謝，居百餘日，乃力疾入直學士院。

translations.literal: But Zai was already ill and could not offer thanks; after more than a hundred days he forced himself, despite illness, to enter duty at the Academicians' Institute.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zai was already ill and unable to offer thanks in person. After more than a hundred days he forced himself, despite his illness, to report for duty at the Hanlin Institute.

sentences.zh: 世宗憐之，賜誥還第，遣太醫視疾。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong took pity on him, granted him the appointment decree and sent him home, and dispatched an imperial physician to attend his illness.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong took pity on him, granted him the appointment decree and sent him home, and dispatched an imperial physician to treat his illness.

sentences.zh: 年三十有六卒。

translations.literal: He died at the age of thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 載始自解褐至終才四年，而與劉袞皆有才無命，時論惜之。

translations.literal: From Zai's first office upon leaving coarse cloth to his end was only four years; both he and Liu Gun had talent but not fate, and contemporary opinion regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: From Zai's first appointment to his death was only four years. Both he and Liu Gun were men of talent cut short by fate, and opinion at the time mourned the loss.

sentences.zh: 劉袞，彭城人。

translations.literal: Liu Gun was a man of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Gun was a native of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 神爽氣俊，富有文藻，繇進士第任左拾遺，與扈載齊名，年二十八而卒。

translations.literal: His spirit was bright and his bearing handsome; he was rich in literary ornament. Through the jinshi degree he was appointed Left Reminder and Reclaimer; he was famed equally with Hu Zai, and died at the age of twenty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He was spirited and handsome, and richly gifted in letters. Having passed the jinshi examination, he was appointed Left Reminder and Reclaimer. He was as celebrated as Hu Zai, and died at the age of twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 賈緯，真定獲鹿人也。

translations.literal: Jia Wei was a man of Huolu in Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Wei was a native of Huolu in Zhending.

translations.literal: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.
translations.idiomatic: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.

sentences.zh: （宋祁《景文集·賈令君墓誌銘》：賈氏自唐司空魏國公耽，世貫滄州南皮，子孫稍稍徙真定。

translations.literal: (Song Qi's 《Collected Works of Jing · Epitaph for Lord Jia》 says: The Jia clan descended from Dan, Duke of Wei and Minister of Works of Tang; for generations they were established at Nanpi in Cang Prefecture, and the descendants gradually moved to Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: (In Song Qi's 《Collected Works of Jing · Epitaph for Lord Jia》, it is written: The Jia clan traced its descent from Dan, Duke of Wei and Minister of Works under Tang. For generations they were established at Nanpi in Cang Prefecture, and the descendants gradually moved to Zhending.

sentences.zh: 五世祖諒，高祖瑾。

translations.literal: The fifth-generation ancestor was Liang; the great-grandfather was Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth-generation ancestor was Liang, and the great-grandfather was Jin.

sentences.zh: 曾祖處士諱初，有至性，疾世方亂，守鄉里，不肯事四方。

translations.literal: The great-grandfather, the retired gentleman whose taboo name was Chu, had utmost sincerity; distressed that the age was in chaos, he kept to his native place and refused to serve in any quarter.
translations.idiomatic: The great-grandfather, the retired gentleman whose taboo name was Chu, was a man of deep filial devotion. Distressed that the world was in turmoil, he remained in his home district and refused to seek office elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 祖諱緯。）〉

translations.literal: The grandfather's taboo name was Wei. )〉
translations.idiomatic: The grandfather's taboo name was Wei.)〉

sentences.zh: 少苦學為文，唐末舉進士不第，遇亂歸河朔，本府累署參軍、邑宰。

translations.literal: In youth he studied writing with hardship; at the end of Tang he attempted the jinshi examination but did not pass. Encountering chaos, he returned to Heshuo, and the local prefecture repeatedly appointed him staff officer and district magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied writing with great diligence. Near the end of Tang he attempted the jinshi examination but failed. When chaos broke out he returned to Heshuo, where the local prefecture repeatedly appointed him as staff officer and district magistrate.

sentences.zh: 唐天成中，範延光鎮定州，表授趙州軍事判官，遷石邑縣令。

translations.literal: In the Tiancheng era of Tang, Fan Yanguang was stationed at Ding Prefecture and memorialized him as military administration judge of Zhao Prefecture; he was promoted to magistrate of Shiyi County.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiancheng era of Tang, Fan Yanguang was military commissioner of Ding Prefecture and recommended him as military administration judge of Zhao Prefecture. He was later promoted to magistrate of Shiyi County.

sentences.zh: 緯屬文之外，勤於撰述，以唐代諸帝實錄，自武宗已下闕而不紀，乃采掇近代傳聞之事，及諸家小說，第其年月，編為《唐年補錄》，凡六十五卷，識者賞之。

translations.literal: Apart from literary composition, Wei was diligent in writing. Because the Veritable Records of the Tang emperors from Emperor Wuzong downward were missing and unrecorded, he gathered recent hearsay and various household tales, arranged them by year and month, and compiled them as the 《Supplemental Annals of the Tang》, altogether sixty-five scrolls; men of discernment praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from his literary work, Wei was diligent in historical writing. Because the Veritable Records of the Tang emperors from Emperor Wuzong onward were lost and unrecorded, he collected recent hearsay and tales from various sources, arranged them chronologically, and compiled the 《Supplemental Annals of the Tang》 in sixty-five scrolls. Men of judgment praised the work.

translations.literal: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.
translations.idiomatic: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.

sentences.zh: （《景文集》：緯博學善詞章，論議明銳，一時諸儒皆屈。

translations.literal: (The 《Collected Works of Jing》 says: Wei was broadly learned and skilled in literary composition; his discourse was sharp and clear, and the Confucian scholars of the age all yielded to him.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Collected Works of Jing》 states: Wei was broadly learned and skilled in letters; his arguments were sharp and incisive, and the leading scholars of the day all yielded before him.

sentences.zh: 唐自武宗後，史錄亡散，君掇拾殘余，為《唐年補錄》數十萬言，敘成敗事甚悉，書顯於時。）〉

translations.literal: From Tang after Wuzong, historical records were lost and scattered; the lord gathered the remnants and made the 《Supplemental Annals of the Tang》, several hundred thousand words, narrating successes and failures very fully; the book was prominent in its time. )〉
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wuzong of Tang, the historical records were lost and scattered. He gathered what remained and produced the 《Supplemental Annals of the Tang》, several hundred thousand words in length, narrating successes and failures in great detail. The book won renown in its day.)〉

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，入為監察御史，改太常博士。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu era of Jin he entered court as investigating censor and was changed to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianfu era of Later Jin he entered court service as investigating censor and was reassigned as Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 緯常以史才自負，銳於編述，不樂曲臺之任，乃陳情於相座。

translations.literal: Wei often prided himself on his talent for history, was keen on compilation, did not delight in the duties of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and therefore presented his feelings to the chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Wei often prided himself on his talent for historiography and was eager to compile historical works. Unhappy with his post at the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, he submitted a personal appeal to the chief minister.

sentences.zh: 又與監修國史趙瑩詩曰：「滿朝唯我相，秉柄無親讎，三年司大董，最切是編修，史才不易得，勤勤處處求。

translations.literal: He also wrote a poem to Zhao Ying, supervisor of the compilation of the National History, saying: "Throughout the court only I am chancellor; wielding power I have no personal enemies; for three years I have directed the great directorate — what is most urgent is compilation; historical talent is not easily obtained — diligently I seek it everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: He also addressed a poem to Zhao Ying, who was supervising compilation of the National History: "In all the court I alone am chancellor, holding power without private grudges. Three years I have overseen the great directorate — and nothing is more pressing than compilation. Men of historiographical talent are hard to come by; I must seek them out tirelessly wherever they may be.

sentences.zh: 愚從年始立，東觀思優遊，昔時人未許，今來虛白頭，春臺與秋閣，往往興歸愁，信運北闕下，不系如虛舟。

translations.literal: I, Wei, from the year I came of age, at the Eastern Pavilion dreamed of leisurely living; in former times men did not approve; now I have grown old in vain; the Spring Terrace and Autumn Pavilion often stir thoughts of return and sorrow; trusting fate beneath the northern palace gate, unmoored like an empty boat.
translations.idiomatic: From the year I came of age, I longed for the leisurely life of the Eastern Pavilion. In those days others would not approve; now my hair has whitened with nothing achieved. At the Spring Terrace and Autumn Pavilion I am often seized by thoughts of home and sorrow. I put my trust in fate beneath the northern gate of the palace, adrift and unmoored like an empty boat.

sentences.zh: 綿蕝非所好，一日疑三秋，何當適所願，便如升瀛洲。

translations.literal: Straw mat and bamboo screen are not what I love; one day feels like three autumns; when will my wish be fulfilled — then it would be like ascending the Isle of Immortals.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial routine at the Court of Sacrifices is not my passion; each day feels as long as three autumns. When will my heart's desire be granted? Then I would be like one ascending the Isles of the Immortals.

sentences.zh: 」未幾，轉屯田員外郎，改起居郎、史館修撰。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Vice Director of the Agriculture Ministry, changed to Court Diarist and Historiography Institute compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Vice Director of the Agriculture Ministry, then reassigned as Court Diarist and compiler at the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 又謂瑩曰：「《唐史》一百三十卷，止於代宗，已下十餘朝未有正史，請與同職修之。

translations.literal: He also said to Ying: "The 《History of Tang》, one hundred thirty scrolls, stops at Emperor Daizong; for more than ten reigns below there is no official history. I ask to compile it together with my colleagues.
translations.idiomatic: He also said to Ying, "The 《History of Tang》, in one hundred thirty scrolls, ends with Emperor Daizong. For more than ten reigns thereafter there is no official history. I ask to compile it together with my colleagues.

sentences.zh: 」瑩以其言上奏，晉祖然之，謂李崧曰：「賈緯欲修《唐史》，如何？

translations.literal: Ying memorialized his words to the throne; the Jin founder approved and said to Li Song: "Jia Wei wishes to compile the 《History of Tang》 — what of it?"
translations.idiomatic: Ying reported his proposal to the throne. The founder of Later Jin approved and asked Li Song, "Jia Wei wishes to compile the 《History of Tang》 — what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣每見史官輩言，唐朝近百年來無實錄，既無根本，安能編紀。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your subject has often heard the historiographers say that for nearly a hundred years Tang has had no Veritable Records; since there is no foundation, how can one compile a chronicle?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Your subject has often heard the historiographers say that for nearly a century Tang has had no Veritable Records. Without a foundation, how can a chronicle be compiled?"

sentences.zh: 」緯聞崧言，頗怒，面責崧沮己。

translations.literal: Wei heard Song's words and was quite angry; to his face he reproached Song for obstructing him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei heard Song's reply he grew angry and openly reproached Song for blocking him.

sentences.zh: 崧曰：「與公鄉人，理須相惜，此事非細，安敢輕言。

translations.literal: Song said: "I am a fellow townsman with you, sir — by principle I ought to cherish you; this matter is not slight — how would I dare speak lightly?"
translations.idiomatic: Song said, "We are fellow townsmen, sir, and by rights I ought to look out for you. This is no small matter — how could I speak lightly?"

sentences.zh: 」緯與宰臣論說不已。

translations.literal: Wei debated with the chief ministers without stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Wei continued arguing with the chief ministers without letup.

sentences.zh: 明年春，敕修《唐史》，緯在籍中。

translations.literal: In spring of the next year an edict ordered compilation of the 《History of Tang》, and Wei was listed among the compilers.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring an edict ordered the compilation of the 《History of Tang》, and Wei was named among the compilers.

sentences.zh: 月餘，丁內艱，歸真定。

translations.literal: After a little more than a month he entered mourning for his mother and returned to Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: A little more than a month later he entered mourning for his mother and returned to Zhending.

sentences.zh: 開運初，服闋，復起居郎，修撰如故，尋以本官知制誥。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyun, when mourning ended, he resumed as Court Diarist with his compiler duties as before, and soon added charge of drafting edicts to his original office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaiyun era, when his mourning period ended, he resumed his post as Court Diarist and continued his work as compiler. Soon afterward he was given charge of drafting edicts in addition to his existing office.

sentences.zh: 緯長於記註，應用文筆，未能過人，而議論剛強，儕類不平之，因目之為「賈鐵嘴」。

translations.literal: Wei was skilled at record-keeping and applied writing, yet could not surpass others; but his discourse was forceful and rigid, and his peers were displeased, so they labeled him "Iron Mouth Jia."
translations.idiomatic: Wei was skilled at record-keeping and practical writing, though not outstanding in either. His opinions, however, were forceful and unyielding, and his colleagues resented him for it, calling him "Iron Mouth Jia."

sentences.zh: 開運中，累遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyun era he was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyun era he was promoted in succession to Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 契丹入京師，隨契丹至真定，後與公卿還朝，授左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When the Khitan entered the capital, he followed the Khitan to Zhending; later he returned to court with the high officials and was appointed Left Grand Master of Remonstrance and Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan entered the capital, he followed them to Zhending. Later he returned to court with the high officials and was appointed Left Grand Master of Remonstrance and Discussion.

sentences.zh: 緯以久次綸閣，比望丞郎之拜，及遷諫署，觖望彌甚。

translations.literal: Wei, because he had long served in the drafting institute, had compared himself to those receiving director and vice director appointments; when he was moved to the remonstrance office, his disappointed ambition grew all the stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Wei had long served in the drafting institute and had expected appointment as a director or vice director. When he was transferred instead to the remonstrance office, his disappointment grew all the sharper.

sentences.zh: 蘇逢吉監修國史，以緯頻投文字，甚知之，尋充史館修撰，判館事。

translations.literal: Su Fengji supervised compilation of the National History; because Wei frequently submitted writings, he knew him well, and soon appointed him Historiography Institute compiler with charge of institute affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Su Fengji, who was supervising compilation of the National History, knew Wei well because Wei frequently submitted writings to him. Soon afterward Wei was appointed Historiography Institute compiler with charge of institute affairs.

sentences.zh: 乾祐中，受詔與王伸、竇儼修漢高祖實錄，緯以筆削為己任，然而褒貶之際，憎愛任情。

translations.literal: In the Qianyou era he received an edict to compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Gaozu of Han together with Wang Shen and Dou Yan. Wei took the brush and editing as his own responsibility, yet in praise and blame he let affection and hatred follow his feelings.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianyou era he received an edict to compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Gaozu of Later Han together with Wang Shen and Dou Yan. Wei took editorial responsibility upon himself, but in matters of praise and blame he let personal likes and dislikes govern his judgment.

sentences.zh: 晉相桑維翰執政日，薄緯之為人，不甚見禮，緯深銜之。

translations.literal: On the days when Jin chancellor Sang Weihan held power, he looked lightly on Wei's character and did not treat him with much courtesy; Wei deeply harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: While the Later Jin chancellor Sang Weihan was in power, he looked down on Wei's character and showed him little courtesy. Wei deeply resented it.

sentences.zh: 及敘《維翰傳》：「身沒之後，有白金八千鋌，他物稱是。

translations.literal: When he came to narrate the 《Biography of Weihan》: "After his death there were eight thousand ingots of white silver, and other goods in proportion."
translations.idiomatic: When he came to write the biography of Weihan, he recorded: "After his death there were eight thousand ingots of white silver, with other goods in proportion."

sentences.zh: 」翰林學士徐臺符，緯邑人也，與緯相善，謂緯曰：「切聞吾友書桑魏公白金之數，不亦多乎！

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Xu Taifu, a fellow townsman of Wei, was on good terms with Wei and said to him: "I have just heard, my friend, that in your writing the Duke of Wei Sang's count of white silver — is it not rather much!"
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Xu Taifu, a fellow townsman of Wei, was on good terms with him and said, "I have just heard, my friend, that in your account the Duke of Wei Sang's hoard of white silver — is it not rather excessive!"

sentences.zh: 但以十目所睹，不可厚誣。

translations.literal: But what the ten eyes have seen — one must not falsely accuse too heavily.
translations.idiomatic: But one must not make so grave a false charge against what many eyes have witnessed.

sentences.zh: 」緯不得已，改為白金數千錠。

translations.literal: Wei had no choice and changed it to several thousand ingots of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: Wei had no choice and changed the figure to several thousand ingots of white silver.

sentences.zh: 趙延乂，字子英，秦州人。

translations.literal: Zhao Yanyi, styled Ziying, was a man of Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanyi, whose style name was Ziying, was a native of Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曾祖省躬，以明術數為通州司馬，遇亂避地於蜀。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Shengong, because he was skilled in numerology and divination, served as Vice Prefect of Tong Prefecture; encountering chaos, he took refuge in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shengong, skilled in numerology and divination, served as Vice Prefect of Tong Prefecture. When chaos broke out he took refuge in Shu.

sentences.zh: 祖師古，黔中經略判官。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shigu was military administration judge under the Qianzhong frontier commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shigu served as military administration judge under the Qianzhong frontier commissioner.

sentences.zh: 父溫珪，仕蜀為司天監。

translations.literal: His father Wengui served Shu as Director of the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wengui served Shu as Director of the Directorate of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 溫珪長於袁、許之術，兼之推步。

translations.literal: Wengui was skilled in the arts of Yuan and Xu, and also in calendrical calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Wengui was skilled in the arts of Yuan Tiangang and Xu Fuxian, and also in calendrical astronomy.

sentences.zh: 王建時，深蒙寵待，延問得失，事微差跌，即被詰讓。

translations.literal: In the time of Wang Jian he was deeply favored; when consulted on gains and losses, if matters fell slightly short he was immediately reproached.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wang Jian he enjoyed deep favor. When consulted on affairs of state, the slightest misstep would bring immediate reproach.

sentences.zh: 臨終謂其子曰：「技術雖是世業，吾仕蜀已來，幾由技術而死，爾輩能以他途致身，亦良圖也。

translations.literal: On his deathbed he said to his sons: "Although these arts are our hereditary profession, since I entered service in Shu I have several times nearly died because of them. If you can achieve standing by another path, that too is a good plan.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he said to his sons, "Although these arts are our family profession, ever since I entered service in Shu I have several times nearly died because of them. If you can make your way in life by some other path, that would be the wiser course.

sentences.zh: 」延乂少以家法仕蜀，由蔭為奉禮部翰林待詔。

translations.literal: Yanyi in youth, through the family profession, entered service in Shu; through inherited privilege he became a Hanlin awaiting edict in the Ceremonial Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Yanyi entered Shu service in youth through the family profession and, by inherited privilege, became a Hanlin awaiting edict in the Ceremonial Ministry.

sentences.zh: 蜀亡入洛，時年三十。

translations.literal: When Shu fell he entered Luoyang, aged thirty.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu fell he went to Luoyang at the age of thirty.

sentences.zh: 天成中，得蜀舊職。

translations.literal: In the Tiancheng era he obtained his former Shu office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiancheng era he recovered his former office from Shu.

sentences.zh: 延乂世為星官，兼通三式，尤長於袁、許之鑒。

translations.literal: Yanyi for generations was an astral officer, and also mastered the Three Methods; he was especially accomplished in the discernment of Yuan and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Yanyi came from a family of astral officers and also mastered the Three Methods of divination. He was especially accomplished in the arts of Yuan and Xu.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，嘗與樞密直學士呂琦同宿於內廷，琦因從容密問國家運祚，延乂曰：「來年厄會之期，俟過別論。

translations.literal: In the Qingtai era he once lodged overnight in the inner court together with Grand Councilor Direct Academician Lu Qi. Qi then, at ease, privately asked about the dynasty's fortune. Yanyi said: "Next year is the term of calamity; wait until it has passed and we may discuss it separately.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingtai era he once lodged overnight in the inner court with Grand Councilor Direct Academician Lu Qi. Qi casually asked him in private about the dynasty's fortunes. Yanyi replied, "Next year is the time of calamity. Wait until it has passed and we may discuss the matter further.

sentences.zh: 」琦訊之不已，延乂曰：「保邦在刑政，保祚在福德。

translations.literal: Qi pressed the inquiry without stopping. Yanyi said: "Preserving the state lies in punishments and government; preserving the dynasty lies in virtue and blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Qi pressed him without letup. Yanyi said, "The preservation of the state depends on law and governance; the preservation of the dynasty depends on virtue and merit.

sentences.zh: 在刑政則術士不敢言，奈際會諸公，罕有卓絕福德者，下官實有恤緯之僭。

translations.literal: In punishments and government the diviners dare not speak; yet among the lords of the age there are rarely men of outstanding virtue and blessing — this lower official truly has the presumption of one who mends a hem in anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: Where law and governance are concerned, diviners dare not speak plainly. Yet among the lords of the age there are few men of outstanding virtue and merit — and I truly overstep in presuming to worry about the fate of the throne.

sentences.zh: 」其年，兼衛尉少卿。

translations.literal: That year he concurrently served as Vice Director of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was concurrently appointed Vice Director of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，代馬重績為司天監。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu era of Jin he replaced Ma Chongji as Director of the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianfu era of Later Jin he succeeded Ma Chongji as Director of the Directorate of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 契丹入京師，隨至鎮州，時契丹滿達勒為帥，會漢高祖定兩京，控鶴都將李筠與諸校密謀劫庫兵，逐契丹，猶豫未決，謀於延乂，因假以術數贊成之。

translations.literal: When the Khitan entered the capital, he followed them to Zhen Prefecture. At that time the Khitan Mandale was commander. When Emperor Gaozu of Han secured the Two Capitals, Commander of the Crane-Control Directorate Li Jun and various officers secretly plotted to seize the arsenal weapons and drive out the Khitan; hesitating and undecided, they consulted Yanyi, and through divination he lent his approval.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan entered the capital, he followed them to Zhen Prefecture, where the Khitan commander Mandale was then in charge. When Emperor Gaozu of Later Han secured the Two Capitals, Li Jun, commander of the Crane-Control Directorate, and several officers secretly plotted to seize weapons from the arsenal and drive out the Khitan. Hesitating and unable to decide, they consulted Yanyi, who used divination to lend his support to the plan.

sentences.zh: 契丹既去，還京師，官秩如舊。

translations.literal: Once the Khitan had departed, he returned to the capital and his rank and office were as before.
translations.idiomatic: After the Khitan withdrew, he returned to the capital and retained his former rank and office.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，加檢校司徒，本官如故，太祖數召對焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he was given the additional title of Honorary Minister of Education; his original office remained as before, and the Founding Emperor repeatedly summoned him for audience.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Guangshun era he was given the additional title of Honorary Minister of Education while retaining his original office. The Founding Emperor repeatedly summoned him for private audience.

translations.literal: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.
translations.idiomatic: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.

sentences.zh: （《歐陽史》：周太祖自魏以兵入京師，召延乂問：「漢祚短促者，天數耶？

translations.literal: (The 《New History of the Five Dynasties》 says: Emperor Taizu of Zhou, leading troops from Wei into the capital, summoned Yanyi and asked: "That the Han dynasty was brief — was it Heaven's decree?"
translations.idiomatic: (The 《New History of the Five Dynasties》 states: When Emperor Taizu of Later Zhou led troops from Wei into the capital, he summoned Yanyi and asked, "Was the brevity of the Han dynasty ordained by Heaven?"

sentences.zh: 」延乂言：「王者撫天下，當以仁恩德澤，而漢淫酷，刑法枉濫，天下稱冤，此其所以亡也。

translations.literal: Yanyi said: "A king who pacifies all under Heaven ought to do so with benevolence, grace, virtue, and favor; yet Han was licentious and cruel, its punishments and laws perverse and excessive, and all under Heaven cried injustice — this is why it perished.
translations.idiomatic: Yanyi replied, "A ruler who governs all under Heaven ought to do so with benevolence, grace, and virtue. Later Han, however, was cruel and excessive; its punishments and laws were perverse and unjust, and the people cried out in grievance. That is why it fell.

sentences.zh: 」是時太祖方以兵圍蘇逢吉、劉銖第，欲誅其族，聞延乂言悚然，因貸其族，二家獲全。）〉

translations.literal: At that time the Founding Emperor was just then surrounding the mansions of Su Fengji and Liu Zhu with troops, intending to exterminate their clans. Hearing Yanyi's words he was struck with dread, and therefore spared their clans; both families were preserved. )〉
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Founding Emperor was besieging the mansions of Su Fengji and Liu Zhu with troops, intending to wipe out their entire clans. When he heard Yanyi's reply he was shaken, and spared both families; the two households were thus saved.)〉

sentences.zh: 延乂善交遊，達機變，兼有技術，見者歡心。

translations.literal: Yanyi was skilled at socializing, understood opportunism, and also possessed technical arts; those who met him were delighted.
translations.idiomatic: Yanyi was skilled at making friends, quick to read changing circumstances, and versed in the technical arts as well; all who met him took to him at once.

sentences.zh: 二年，授太府卿，判司天監事。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Grand Steward of the Treasury with charge of Directorate of Astronomy affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed Grand Steward of the Treasury and given charge of the Directorate of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 其年夏初，火犯靈臺，延乂自言星官所忌，又言身命宮災並，未幾其子卒，尋又妻卒，俄而延乂嬰疾，故人省之，舉手曰：「多謝諸親，死災不可逭也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of summer that year, fire trespassed upon the Observatory Platform. Yanyi himself said it was what astral officers dread, and also said calamity would strike both his body and life palaces. Before long his son died; soon after his wife died as well. Shortly afterward Yanyi fell ill. When old friends visited him, he raised his hand and said: "Many thanks to you all, my kin — the calamity of death cannot be evaded.
translations.idiomatic: Early that summer, Mars trespassed upon the Observatory Platform. Yanyi declared that this was an omen dreaded by astral officers and predicted that calamity would strike both his body and life palaces. Before long his son died; soon his wife died as well. Shortly afterward Yanyi himself fell gravely ill. When old friends came to visit, he raised his hand and said, "My thanks to you all — the calamity of death cannot be escaped.

sentences.zh: 」尋卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: Before long he died, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward at the age of fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈光祿卿。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title of Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 沈遘，字期遠，睢陽人也。

translations.literal: Shen Gou, styled Qiyuan, was a man of Suiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Gou, whose style name was Qiyuan, was a native of Suiyang.

sentences.zh: 父振，貝州永濟令，累贈左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: His father Zhen was magistrate of Yongji in Bei Prefecture and was repeatedly posthumously granted Left Grand Master of Remonstrance and Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhen had been magistrate of Yongji in Bei Prefecture and was posthumously granted the title of Left Grand Master of Remonstrance and Discussion.

sentences.zh: 遘幼孤，以苦學為誌，弱冠登進士第，釋褐除校書郎，由御史臺主簿拜監察御史，凡五遷至金部郎中，充三司判官。

translations.literal: Gou was orphaned in youth and took arduous study as his aim.
