At the capping age he passed the jinshi examination, upon leaving coarse cloth was appointed collator, from chief clerk of the Censorate was invested as investigating censor, and in five promotions reached Director of the Gold Ministry, serving as judge of the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Gou lost his father while still young and devoted himself to rigorous study. He passed the jinshi examination in his early twenties, took his first office as collator, rose from chief clerk of the Censorate to investigating censor, and after five promotions reached Director of the Gold Ministry, serving as judge of the Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 廣順中，以本官知制誥。

translations.literal: In the Guangshun era he added charge of drafting edicts to his original office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangshun era he was given charge of drafting edicts in addition to his existing office.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，擢為翰林院學士，歲滿，拜中書舍人充職。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong succeeded to the throne, he was promoted to Hanlin Academician; when his term expired he was invested as Secretariat Drafter while retaining that duty.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong succeeded to the throne, he was promoted to Hanlin Academician. When his term expired he was appointed Secretariat Drafter while continuing in that role.

sentences.zh: 顯德三年夏，以扈從南征，因為遇疾歸，及京而卒。

translations.literal: In summer of the third year of Xiande, while attending the southern campaign he fell ill and returned home; upon reaching the capital he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the third year of Xiande, while accompanying the southern campaign he fell ill and returned home, and died upon reaching the capital.

sentences.zh: 遘為人謙和，勤於接下，每文士投贄，必擇其賢者而譽之，故當時後進之士多歸焉。

translations.literal: Gou as a man was modest and harmonious, diligent in receiving those below him. Whenever literary men submitted presentation pieces, he always chose the worthy among them and praised them; therefore the rising scholars of the age mostly gravitated to him.
translations.idiomatic: Gou was modest and gracious, and diligent in welcoming those beneath him. Whenever literary men submitted presentation pieces, he always singled out the worthy ones for praise, and for this reason many rising scholars of the day sought his patronage.

sentences.zh: 李知損，字化機，大梁人也。

translations.literal: Li Zhisun, styled Huaji, was a man of Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhisun, whose style name was Huaji, was a native of Daliang.

sentences.zh: 少輕薄，利口無行。

translations.literal: In youth he was frivolous, sharp-tongued, and without propriety.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was frivolous, sharp-tongued, and utterly lacking in propriety.

sentences.zh: 梁朝時，以牒刺篇詠出入於內臣之門，繇是浪得虛譽，時人目之為「李羅隱」。

translations.literal: In the Liang dynasty, by posting poems and verses he came and went at the gates of inner courtiers; thereby he vainly obtained empty reputation, and men of the age labeled him "Li Luo Yin."
translations.idiomatic: During the Liang dynasty he circulated poems and verses among the inner courtiers, and through these connections he acquired an undeserved reputation. People of the day nicknamed him "Li Luo Yin."

sentences.zh: 為累藩鎮從事，入拜左補闕，歷刑部兵二員外、度支判官、右司郎中。

translations.literal: He successively served as staff officer under several military commissioners, entered court as Left Remonstrance and Supplementation Officer, and successively served as vice director of the Punishments and War ministries, judge of the Revenue Office, and Director of the Right Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as staff officer under several military commissioners, entered court as Left Remonstrance and Supplementation Officer, and later held the posts of vice director of the Ministries of Punishments and War, judge of the Revenue Office, and Director of the Right Bureau.

sentences.zh: 坐受榷鹽使王景遇厚賂，謫於均州。

translations.literal: Because he accepted heavy bribes from salt monopoly commissioner Wang Jingyu, he was demoted to Jun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After accepting heavy bribes from salt monopoly commissioner Wang Jingyu, he was demoted and sent to Jun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 漢初歸朝，除右司郎中，兼侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han he returned to court, was appointed Director of the Right Bureau, and concurrently served as attendant censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Later Han he returned to court, was appointed Director of the Right Bureau, and concurrently served as attendant censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs.

sentences.zh: 廣順中，拜右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In the Guangshun era he was invested as Right Grand Master of Remonstrance and Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangshun era he was appointed Right Grand Master of Remonstrance and Discussion.

sentences.zh: 時王峻為樞密使，知損以與峻有舊，遂指峻求使於江浙，峻為上言。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Jun was Grand Councilor. Zhisun, because he had old ties with Jun, then pointed to Jun and requested an envoy post to Jiang and Zhe; Jun spoke of it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Jun was Grand Councilor. Zhisun, having old ties with Jun, asked Jun to recommend him for an envoy mission to Jiangsu and Zhejiang, and Jun put the request before the throne.

sentences.zh: 太祖素聞知損所為，甚難之。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor had long heard of Zhisun's conduct and found it very difficult to approve.
translations.idiomatic: The Founding Emperor had long known of Zhisun's reputation and was deeply reluctant to approve the appointment.

sentences.zh: 峻曰：「此人如或辱命，譴之可也。

translations.literal: Jun said: "If this man should disgrace the mission, he can be punished for it.
translations.idiomatic: Jun said, "If this man disgraces the mission, he can always be punished afterward.

sentences.zh: 」太祖重違其請，遂可之。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor, loath to refuse his request, then approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to refuse Jun's request outright, the Founding Emperor approved the appointment.

sentences.zh: 知損既受命，大恣其荒誕之意，遂假資於人，廣備行李。

translations.literal: Once Zhisun had received his commission, he greatly indulged his absurd whims, borrowed money from others, and lavishly prepared his baggage.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhisun received his commission, he gave free rein to his absurd impulses, borrowing money from others and lavishly outfitting his entourage.

sentences.zh: 及即路，所經州郡，無不強貸，又移書於青州符彥卿，借錢百萬。

translations.literal: When he set out on the road, in every prefecture and district he passed through he forced loans without exception, and also sent a letter to Fu Yanqing in Qing Prefecture borrowing a million in cash.
translations.idiomatic: Once on the road, he extorted loans in every prefecture and district he passed through, and even sent a letter to Fu Yanqing in Qing Prefecture demanding a loan of a million in cash.

sentences.zh: 及在郵亭，行止穢雜。

translations.literal: When at courier stations, his conduct was filthy and disorderly.
translations.idiomatic: At courier stations his behavior was vulgar and disorderly in the extreme.

sentences.zh: 王峻聞而奏之，乃責授棣州司馬。

translations.literal: Wang Jun heard of it and memorialized the throne; he was then demoted and appointed military adjutant at Di Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jun heard of this he reported it to the throne, and Zhisun was demoted to military adjutant at Di Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，切於求人，素聞知損狂狷，好上封事，謂有可采，且欲聞外事，即命征還，遽與復資。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong acceded to the throne, he was eager to seek out men. He had long heard that Zhisun was wild and obstinate and fond of submitting sealed memorials; thinking there might be something worth taking from them, and wishing also to hear of outside affairs, he immediately ordered him recalled and promptly restored his rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong acceded to the throne, he was eager to recruit talent. He had long heard that Zhisun was eccentric and outspoken, fond of submitting sealed memorials that might contain something useful, and wishing to hear news from beyond the capital, he ordered Zhisun recalled and promptly restored his rank.

sentences.zh: 數月之間，日貢章疏，多斥讟貴近，自謀進取，又上章求為過海使。

translations.literal: Within a few months he daily submitted memorials, mostly denouncing those close to power, scheming for his own advancement; he also submitted a memorial requesting appointment as envoy across the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months he submitted memorials daily, mostly denouncing those close to power while angling for his own advancement. He also petitioned to be appointed envoy across the sea.

sentences.zh: 世宗因發怒，仍以其醜行日彰，故命除名，配沙門島。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong therefore grew angry, and because his disgraceful conduct grew daily more evident, ordered his name struck from the rolls and sent him in exile to Shamen Island.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong flew into a rage. Because Zhisun's disgraceful conduct was growing more notorious by the day, he ordered his name struck from the rolls and sent him into exile on Shamen Island.

sentences.zh: 知損將行，謂所親曰：「余嘗遇善相者，言我三逐之後，當居相位，余自此而三矣，子姑待我。

translations.literal: As Zhisun was about to depart, he said to those close to him: "I once met a skilled physiognomist who said that after three banishments I would hold the chancellorship. From this point I have reached the third — you had best wait for me.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhisun was about to depart, he told his intimates, "I once met a skilled physiognomist who said that after three banishments I would reach the chancellorship. This makes the third — you had best wait for me.

sentences.zh: 」後歲餘，卒於海中，其庸誕也如此。

translations.literal: A little more than a year later he died at sea — his absurdity was just like this.
translations.idiomatic: A little more than a year later he died at sea. Such was the measure of his absurd self-delusion.

translations.literal: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.
translations.idiomatic: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.

sentences.zh: （《五代史補》：李知損，官至諫議大夫，好輕薄，時人謂之「李羅隱」。

translations.literal: (The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》 says: Li Zhisun rose to Grand Master of Remonstrance and Discussion, loved frivolity, and men of the age called him "Li Luo Yin."
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》 states: Li Zhisun rose to Grand Master of Remonstrance and Discussion. Fond of frivolity, he was known to his contemporaries as "Li Luo Yin."

sentences.zh: 至於親友間往還簡牘，往往引裏巷常談，謂之偶對。

translations.literal: In letters exchanged among kin and friends, he often cited common alley talk and called it paired couplets.
translations.idiomatic: In letters exchanged among friends and relatives, he often quoted street slang and passed it off as witty couplets.

sentences.zh: 常有朝士奉使回，以土物為贈，其意猶望卻回。

translations.literal: There was once a court gentleman returning from a mission who gave him local products as a gift, still hoping they would be sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Once a court official returning from a mission gave him local products as a gift, still expecting them to be returned.

sentences.zh: 知損覺之，且貽書謝之曰：「在小子一時間卻擬送去，恐大官兩羅裏更不將來。

translations.literal: Zhisun perceived this and also sent a letter of thanks saying: "For the moment this petty fellow planned to send them back, but I fear the grand official's two nets will not bring them again.
translations.idiomatic: Zhisun saw through the gesture and sent a letter of thanks saying, "For the moment I had planned to send them back, but I fear Your Excellency's two nets will not bring them round again."

sentences.zh: 」乾祐中，奉使鄭州，時宋彥筠為節度。

translations.literal: In the Qianyou era he was sent on mission to Zheng Prefecture, when Song Yanyun was military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianyou era he was sent on mission to Zheng Prefecture, where Song Yanyun was then military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 彥筠小字忙兒，因宴會，彥筠酒酣，輒問曰：「眾人何為號足下為羅隱？

translations.literal: Yanyun's childhood name was Mang'er. At a banquet, when Yanyun was deep in wine, he abruptly asked: "Why do people call you Luo Yin?"
translations.idiomatic: Yanyun's childhood name was Busy Boy. At a banquet, when Yanyun was well into his cups, he suddenly asked, "Why do people call you Luo Yin?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「下官平素好為詩，其格致大抵如羅隱，故人為號。

translations.literal: He replied: "This lower official has always loved writing poetry; its style and tone are generally like Luo Yin — therefore people gave me the name.
translations.idiomatic: Zhisun replied, "I have always loved writing poetry, and my style is generally like that of Luo Yin — that is why people gave me the nickname.

sentences.zh: 」彥筠曰：「不然，蓋為足下輕薄如羅隱耳。

translations.literal: Yanyun said: "Not so — it is because you, sir, are as frivolous as Luo Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Yanyun said, "Not at all — it is because you are as frivolous as Luo Yin himself.

sentences.zh: 」知損大怒，厲聲曰：「只如令公，人皆謂之宋忙兒，未必便能放牛。

translations.literal: Zhisun grew greatly angry and said in a harsh voice: "Take Your Lordship — everyone calls you Song Busy Boy, but that hardly means you can actually tend cattle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhisun flew into a rage and said sharply, "Take Your Lordship — everyone calls you Song Busy Boy, but that hardly means you can actually herd cattle.

sentences.zh: 」滿座皆笑。）〉

translations.literal: The whole company burst into laughter. )〉
translations.idiomatic: The whole table erupted in laughter.)〉

sentences.zh: 孫晟，本名鳳。

translations.literal: Sun Shen, original name Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shen's original name was Feng.

translations.literal: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.
translations.idiomatic: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.

sentences.zh: （《南唐書》云：孫忌，高密人，一名鳳，又名晟，少舉進士。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Book of Southern Tang》 says: Sun Ji was a man of Gaomi; one name was Feng, another name was Shen; in youth he passed the jinshi examination. )〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Book of Southern Tang》 states: Sun Ji was a native of Gaomi. One of his names was Feng, another was Shen. In youth he passed the jinshi examination.)〉

sentences.zh: 性陰賊，好奸謀。

translations.literal: By nature he was sinister and treacherous, fond of wicked plotting.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was sinister and treacherous, and fond of wicked scheming.

sentences.zh: 少為道士，工詩，於廬山簡寂觀畫唐詩人賈島像，懸於屋壁，以禮事之。

translations.literal: In youth he was a Daoist priest, skilled at poetry. At the Jianji Abbey on Mount Lu he painted a portrait of the Tang poet Jia Dao, hung it on the wall of his room, and served it with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was a Daoist priest and skilled at poetry. At the Jianji Abbey on Mount Lu he painted a portrait of the Tang poet Jia Dao, hung it on his wall, and worshipped it with full ritual ceremony.

sentences.zh: 觀主以為妖妄，執杖驅出之，大為時輩所嗤。

translations.literal: The abbey master regarded this as demonic delusion, took a staff and drove him out, and he was greatly mocked by contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: The abbey master regarded this as demonic folly, took a staff, and drove him out. He became an object of widespread ridicule among his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 改儒服，謁唐莊宗於鎮州，授秘書省著作郎。

translations.literal: He changed to Confucian dress, presented himself to Tang Emperor Zhuangzong at Zhen Prefecture, and was appointed Author at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He exchanged his Daoist robes for Confucian dress, presented himself to Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang at Zhen Prefecture, and was appointed Author at the Secretariat.

translations.literal: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.
translations.idiomatic: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.

sentences.zh: （《南唐書》云：豆盧革為相，雅知忌，辟為判官。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Book of Southern Tang》 says: When Doulu Ge became chancellor, he knew Ji well by reputation and recruited him as military administration judge. )〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Book of Southern Tang》 states: When Doulu Ge became chancellor, he knew Ji well by reputation and recruited him as military administration judge.)〉

sentences.zh: 天成初，朱守殷據夷門叛，時晟為幕賓，贊成其事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng, Zhu Shouyin held Yimen in rebellion; at that time Shen was a staff adviser and helped bring the affair about.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tiancheng era, Zhu Shouyin rebelled and seized Yimen. Shen was then a staff adviser and helped bring the rebellion about.

sentences.zh: 是時晟常擐甲露刃，以十數騎自隨，巡行於市，多所屠害，汴人為之切齒。

translations.literal: At that time Shen often donned armor with bared blade, followed by a dozen or so horsemen, and patrolled the markets, slaughtering many; the people of Bian gnashed their teeth at him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shen often rode through the markets in armor with blade bared, followed by a dozen horsemen, slaughtering many along the way. The people of Bian gnashed their teeth at the very mention of his name.

sentences.zh: 城陷，朱氏被誅，晟乃匿跡更名，棄其妻子，亡命於陳、宋間。

translations.literal: When the city fell, the Zhu clan was executed. Shen then hid his tracks, changed his name, abandoned his wife and children, and fled for his life between Chen and Song.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell the Zhu clan was executed. Shen then went into hiding, changed his name, abandoned his wife and children, and fled for his life between Chen and Song.

translations.literal: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.
translations.idiomatic: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.

sentences.zh: （《歐陽史》云：安重誨惡晟，以為教守殷反者晟也，畫其像購之，不可得，遂族其家。

translations.literal: (The 《New History of the Five Dynasties》 says: An Chonghui hated Shen, believing that the one who had incited Shouyin to rebel was Shen; he had his portrait painted and offered a reward for him, but could not obtain him, and therefore exterminated his clan.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《New History of the Five Dynasties》 states: An Chonghui hated Shen, believing him to have incited Shouyin's rebellion. He had Shen's portrait painted and offered a reward for his capture, but could not find him, and therefore exterminated his entire clan.

sentences.zh: 晟奔於吳。）〉

translations.literal: Shen fled to Wu. )〉
translations.idiomatic: Shen fled to Wu.)〉

sentences.zh: 會同惡者送之過淮，吳人方納叛亡，即以偽官授之。

translations.literal: He happened to meet wicked men who escorted him across the Huai; the Wu people were then receiving defectors and fugitives, and immediately invested him with a puppet office.
translations.idiomatic: He happened upon wicked men who helped him cross the Huai. The Wu court was then accepting defectors and fugitives, and immediately granted him a puppet office.

sentences.zh: 晟亦微有詞翰，李昇偽尊楊溥為讓皇之冊文，即晟之詞也，故江南尤重之。

translations.literal: Shen also had some slight gift for literary composition; the investiture document by which Li Sheng falsely honored Yang Pu as abdicated emperor was Shen's wording, and therefore Jiangnan especially valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Shen also had some gift for literary composition. The investiture document by which Li Sheng falsely honored Yang Pu as abdicated emperor was written in Shen's words, and for this reason Jiangnan held him in particular esteem.

sentences.zh: 二十年間，累歷偽任，財貨邸第，頗適其意。

translations.literal: Over twenty years he successively held puppet appointments; wealth, goods, and mansions largely suited his wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Over twenty years he held a series of puppet appointments, accumulating wealth and mansions that largely suited his tastes.

sentences.zh: 晟以家妓甚眾，每食不設食機，令眾妓各執一食器，周侍於其側，謂之「肉臺盤」，其自養稱愜也如是。

translations.literal: Shen had very many household courtesans. At each meal he set out no dining table, but ordered the courtesans each to hold a food vessel and attend in a circle at his side — this he called the "Flesh Platter." His self-indulgence and contentment were just like this.
translations.idiomatic: Shen kept a large household of courtesans. At each meal he dispensed with a dining table and had the courtesans each hold a food vessel and attend him in a circle — a arrangement he called the "Flesh Platter." Such was the measure of his self-indulgence.

translations.idiomatic: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.

sentences.zh: （《南唐書》云：忌為舒州節度使，治軍嚴，有歸化卒二人，正晝挺白刃入府，求忌殺之。

translations.literal: (The 《Book of Southern Tang》 says: Ji was military commissioner of Shu Prefecture and governed the army strictly. Two surrendered soldiers, in broad daylight, drew bare blades and entered the headquarters seeking to kill Ji.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Book of Southern Tang》 states: Ji was military commissioner of Shu Prefecture and governed his troops with strict discipline. Two surrendered soldiers drew bare blades in broad daylight, entered headquarters, and sought to kill him.

sentences.zh: 入自西門，吏士倉卒莫能禦。

translations.literal: Entering from the west gate, the clerks and soldiers in the haste of the moment could not repel them.
translations.idiomatic: They entered through the west gate, and in the sudden confusion none of the clerks or soldiers could stop them.

sentences.zh: 適忌閑行在東門，聞亂，得民家馬乘之，奔桐城。

translations.literal: Ji happened to be strolling at the east gate. Hearing the disturbance, he obtained a commoner's horse, mounted it, and fled to Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ji happened to be taking a leisurely walk at the east gate. Hearing the commotion, he seized a commoner's horse, mounted it, and fled to Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 叛卒不得忌，乃殺都押衙李建崇而逸。

translations.literal: The mutinous soldiers could not obtain Ji, so they killed Chief Military Aide Li Jianchong and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to catch Ji, the mutinous soldiers killed Chief Military Aide Li Jianchong and fled.

sentences.zh: 忌坐貶光祿卿。）〉

translations.literal: Ji was demoted by association to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness. )〉
translations.idiomatic: Ji was demoted by association to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.)〉

sentences.zh: 顯德三年春，王師下廣陵，江左驚窘，李景偽署晟為司空，令奉貢於行在，世宗遣右常侍劉悅伴之，賜與甚厚。

translations.literal: In spring of the third year of Xiande, the imperial army descended on Guangling; the left bank of the Yangtze was alarmed and distressed. Li Jing falsely appointed Shen Minister of Works and ordered him to present tribute at the imperial camp. Emperor Shizong sent Right Regular Attendant Liu Yue to accompany him and bestowed gifts very generously.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year of Xiande, the imperial army marched on Guangling and threw the Jiangnan region into alarm. Li Jing appointed Shen Minister of Works and ordered him to present tribute at the imperial camp. Emperor Shizong sent Right Regular Attendant Liu Yue to accompany him and lavished generous gifts upon him.

sentences.zh: 洎隨駕到闕，舍於都亭驛，禮遇殊優。

translations.literal: When he followed the imperial carriage to the capital, he lodged at the Capital Pavilion Station and received exceptionally fine courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When he followed the imperial procession to the capital, he was lodged at the Capital Pavilion Station and treated with exceptional courtesy.

sentences.zh: 每召見，飲之醇醴，問以江南事，晟但言：「吳畏陛下之神武，唯以北面為求，保無二也。

translations.literal: Whenever summoned for audience, he was given fine wine and questioned about Jiangnan affairs. Shen only said: "Wu fears Your Majesty's divine martial prowess and seeks only to face north in submission — I guarantee there is no second intent.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever summoned to audience he was given fine wine and questioned about affairs in Jiangnan. Shen would only say, "Wu fears Your Majesty's divine martial prowess and seeks only to submit and face north — I guarantee there is no treachery.

sentences.zh: 」先是，張永德守下蔡，素與李重進不協，每宴將校，多暴其短。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhang Yongde was defending Xiacai and had long been on bad terms with Li Chongjin; whenever he feasted the officers he often exposed Chongjin's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Zhang Yongde was defending Xiacai, he had long been at odds with Li Chongjin. At banquets with his officers he often aired Chongjin's faults.

sentences.zh: 一日，永德乘醉，乃大言重進潛蓄奸謀，當時將校無不驚駭，繇是人情大擾。

translations.literal: One day Yongde, taking advantage of drunkenness, then loudly declared that Chongjin secretly harbored treacherous designs; at the time the officers were all startled and alarmed, and from this popular sentiment was greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: One day, while drunk, Yongde loudly declared that Chongjin was secretly plotting treason. The officers were all shocked, and morale was thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 後密遣親信乘驛上言，世宗不聽，亦不介意。

translations.literal: Later he secretly sent a trusted follower by courier post to report to the throne; Emperor Shizong did not listen and also did not take it to heart.
translations.idiomatic: Later he secretly sent a trusted follower by courier to report to the throne, but Emperor Shizong paid no heed and was not concerned.

sentences.zh: 一日，重進自壽陽去其部從，直指永德帳下，宴飲終日而去，自此人情稍安。

translations.literal: One day Chongjin left his staff at Shouyang, went straight to Yongde's headquarters, feasted and drank all day, then departed; from this popular sentiment gradually calmed.
translations.idiomatic: One day Chongjin left his staff at Shouyang, went straight to Yongde's headquarters, feasted with him all day, and then departed. From that point morale gradually settled.

sentences.zh: 時李景覘而知之，因密令人賫蠟書遺重進，勸為不軌，重進以其蠟書進呈，世宗覽之，皆斥讟反間之言。

translations.literal: At that time Li Jing observed and learned of this, and therefore secretly sent someone bearing a wax-sealed letter to Chongjin urging him to commit treason. Chongjin presented the wax-sealed letter to the throne; Emperor Shizong read it — all were words of slander and subversion.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing learned of this and secretly sent someone bearing a wax-sealed letter to Chongjin, urging him to rebel. Chongjin presented the letter to the throne. Emperor Shizong read it and saw that every word was slander meant to sow discord.

sentences.zh: 世宗怒晟前言失實，因急召侍衛都虞候韓通令收晟下獄，與其從者百餘人皆誅之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong grew angry that Shen's earlier words had been false, and therefore urgently summoned Palace Guard Commandant Han Tong and ordered Shen seized and imprisoned; together with more than a hundred of his followers, all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong, enraged that Shen's earlier assurances had been false, urgently summoned Palace Guard Commandant Han Tong and ordered Shen seized and imprisoned. Shen and more than a hundred of his followers were all executed.

translations.idiomatic: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.

sentences.zh: （《南唐書》云：世宗命都承旨曹翰護至右軍巡院，猶飲之酒，數酌，翰起曰：「相公得罪，賜自盡。

translations.literal: (The 《Book of Southern Tang》 says: Emperor Shizong ordered Chief Palace Aide Cao Han to escort him to the Right Army Patrol Court, still gave him wine, and after several cups Han rose and said: "My lord, you have offended and are granted death by your own hand.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Book of Southern Tang》 states: Emperor Shizong ordered Chief Palace Aide Cao Han to escort him to the Right Army Patrol Court. Wine was still offered, and after several cups Han rose and said, "My lord, you have given offense and are granted the privilege of taking your own life.

sentences.zh: 」忌怡然整衣索笏，東南望再拜曰：「臣受恩深，謹以死謝。

translations.literal: Ji calmly straightened his robes, sought his tablet, bowed twice facing southeast, and said: "Your subject has received deep grace — I respectfully take death in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Ji calmly straightened his robes, took up his court tablet, bowed twice toward the southeast, and said, "I have received deep grace from the throne — I accept death in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 」從者二百人，亦皆誅死於東相國寺。）〉

translations.literal: Two hundred followers were also all executed at the Eastern Xiangguo Temple. )〉
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred of his followers were also executed at the Eastern Xiangguo Temple.)〉

sentences.zh: 翌日，宰臣上謁，世宗親諭之，始知其事實。

translations.literal: The next day the chief ministers attended audience; Emperor Shizong personally informed them, and they then learned the truth of the affair.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the chief ministers attended audience, and Emperor Shizong personally explained the matter to them. Only then did they learn what had actually happened.

sentences.zh: 議者以晟昔構禍於梁民，令伏法於梁獄，報應之道，豈徒然哉！

translations.literal: Commentators held that since Shen had once wrought calamity upon the people of Liang, and now met the law in a Liang prison, the way of retribution — how could it be in vain!
translations.idiomatic: Commentators observed that since Shen had once brought calamity upon the people of Liang, it was only fitting that he should meet the law in a Liang prison. The way of retribution — could it be mere coincidence!

sentences.zh: 晟性慷慨，常感李景之厚遇，誓死以報之。

translations.literal: Shen by nature was generous and forthright; he often felt Li Jing's generous treatment and swore to repay it with his death.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was by nature generous and forthright. Deeply moved by Li Jing's generous treatment of him, he had sworn to repay that kindness with his life.

translations.literal: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.
translations.idiomatic: Opening angle bracket marking the start of an editorial note.

sentences.zh: （《釣磯立談》云：晟將命周朝，自知不免，私謂副使王崇質曰：「吾思之熟矣，終不忍負永陵一壞土，余非所知也。」）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Standing Discourse from the Fishing Platform》 says: When Shen was about to take his commission to the Zhou court, knowing he would not escape, he privately said to Vice Envoy Wang Chongzhi: "I have thought this through thoroughly. In the end I cannot bear to betray a clod of earth of Yongling — that is not something you can understand.")〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Standing Discourse from the Fishing Platform》 states: When Shen was about to depart on his mission to the Zhou court, knowing he would not survive, he privately told Vice Envoy Wang Chongzhi, "I have thought this through carefully. In the end I cannot bring myself to betray even a clod of earth from Yongling — that is something beyond your understanding.")〉

sentences.zh: 及將下獄，世宗令近臣問以江南可取之狀，晟默然不對。

translations.literal: When he was about to be imprisoned, Emperor Shizong ordered a close minister to ask him about the conditions under which Jiangnan could be taken; Shen was silent and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to be imprisoned, Emperor Shizong ordered a close minister to ask him how Jiangnan might be conquered. Shen remained silent and would not answer.

sentences.zh: 臨刑之際，整其衣冠，南望金陵再拜而言曰：「臣惟以死謝。

translations.literal: At the moment of execution he straightened his cap and robes, bowed twice facing south toward Jinling, and said: "Your subject can only repay with death.
translations.idiomatic: At the moment of execution he straightened his cap and robes, bowed twice toward Jinling in the south, and said, "Your subject can repay only with his death.

sentences.zh: 」遂伏誅。

translations.literal: He then submitted to execution.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted to execution.
